results.title: Dia Browser | Stash your PiP out of the way
results.content:
# Stash your PiP out of the way

We’re all constantly doing the dance. You’re multitasking in a meeting (or watching a video) with our nice picture-in-picture window, you go to read something underneath it, and then you spend the next five minutes dragging that window around the screen trying to find a spot where it isn't in the way.

Now, you can stash it. Drag a video or meeting PIP window off to the side of your screen and it sits neatly out of the way, still one click (or drag) from coming back into view. Keep your video close by, without sacrificing the screen real estate.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/3a121e90f463b51e2f640b233ad91559f679c9b7-512x512.png)
Shipped by

Adam

Other ways to stay focused with Dia

**⌘-S to zone in.** In case you didn’t know, using the keyboard shortcut command-s hides your tab bar, so you can really zone in on whatever you’re working on. Tap command-s again to bring it back!

****

**⌘-Click to stick together.** The next time you’re diving deep on a research kick, use command-click to select all the tabs you just opened, and then right click to turn them into a tab group. Once the group is opened, Command-Option-T creates a new tab inside the group, so you can keep all your research in one place!

****

**Meeting Tab Groups reduce the scatter.** When you join a meeting (from a calendar preview or meeting reminder), Dia auto-creates a dedicated tab group for that meeting and keeps the meeting tab anchored so it’s easy to find.⁠⁠ As you open meeting-related links (invite links, agenda/docs/boards/tickets, etc.), Dia drops them into that same meeting’s group so everything for the call stays together.

### Offtheclock

I’m from Minas Gerais, Brazil — the state Brazilians themselves will tell you has the best food in the country. Living in the US, I’ve held onto that identity the best way I know: by throwing parties. Every year, my birthday has become a tradition where nearly a hundred friends and family show up for a full spread of Brazilian music, food and drinks — my wife makes the feijoada (the national dish of Brazil), I’m on caipirinha duty, and between the two of us, nobody leaves hungry ***or*** thirsty.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/4f69ff3c1982c9d3d100209cf169e488f2be475a-510x502.png)
Braised by

Renato

A few more updates

**Every Chrome bookmark makes the move.** Dia now imports bookmarks from Chrome's account file too, so managed and enterprise Google users bring all of them along automatically.
*Shipped by Seb*

****

**Tab groups stick around.** We fixed a bug where tab groups could unexpectedly get deleted if you’re using sync.
*Fixed by Luan*

****

**Close tabs in a snap.** Dia handles closing tabs in a more performant way, so that when you close out a tab, you can instantly move on with your day!
*Improved by Seb*

Behind the design

Last week, our designer Christine shared a bit about her process this Spring. We think you’ll enjoy following [her journey](https://x.com/chrstnerode/status/2065070625970946175?s=20) as she attempts to design**** the polar opposite of AI-generated design.

results.title: Dia Browser | Notes from the roadmap
results.content:
For those who have been waiting, they're finally here. For those who are newer to Dia, **context switching just got a lot simpler**.

Profiles keep your logins, your tools, your AI, your context, exactly where they belong. The missing piece was getting between them quickly. So we added a better way to context switch.

**To try it:** right-click on the tab bar, create a new Profile, and swipe away.

P.S. Curious how we landed here? **Check out** with the design minds behind the swipe.

results.title: Dia Browser | Closing out the week with Dia
results.content:
# Closing out the week with Dia

For some of us, this Thursday is the last workday before a long weekend. Long weekend or not, all weeks come to a close, and we'd rather end them tidy than with work still on our plate. Here's how a few of us clear the deck before the week’s close.

Tara rounds up everything she flagged with 👀

All week I react to Slack messages with the 👀 emoji when I want to come back to something. At the end of the day I ask Dia to pull and prioritize everything I marked into a single report. No scrolling, no hunting through channels — my loose ends, ranked and in one place.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/acae7362dcb2fbceb669a5b07387b052a246142a-430x468.png)
prioritized by

Tara

Dustin asks who's still waiting on him.

Before I shut my laptop, I ask Dia: who do I still owe a reply to, and what did I commit to that I haven’t finished yet. It reads across my Slack, Gmail, and Notion and tells me where the ball's in my court, so I can clear those before I log off.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/6649fdec921707ab7c9654a0c32b282fb91f51f2-512x512.jpg)
cleared by

Dustin

Kyle lets the Morning Brief guide his whole day.

Even though it’s called the Morning Brief, I actually use it all day long. The to-do list is pinpoint accurate for me, and I'll hover over my morning brief tab throughout to see my to-dos at a glance, checking them off as I go.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/454b934ded2c0358887b691fad33c6b25c48afc6-740x654.jpg)
navigated by

Kyle

### GetyourMorningBrief

Go into **Settings > Apps** and turn **New Chat** on. Connect your tools and you'll receive your first one tomorrow. (We need Slack at a minimum, but connect more for a richer brief!)

A few more updates

**Out of sight, automatically off your mind.** New Tab Pages you've drifted away from now clear themselves when you switch apps or lock your screen, so your sidebar stays tidy.
*Shipped by Rishi*

**More than one workspace? Take your pick.** Choose which Slack or Notion workspace your tools work in, right from App settings.
*Shipped by Ali and Rosey*

**Read all about it.** Dia's release notes now land dressed up like a newspaper. All the news that's fit to ship!
*Shipped by Kasper*

### OffTheClock

Lately I've gotten into collecting perfume. Here's my July favorites perfume tray, including some recent and fun highlight additions to the collection:

**Debaser in Bloom by D.S. & Durga:** A white floral featuring a cassette tape note. Smells like warm VCR. Sounds crazy, but its true.

**Moth by Zoologist:** All their perfumes are based on animals. This one was challenging and hard to find an occasion to wear.

**New Eden by House of Cosmo:** Supposed to smell like a breath of fresh air on a lush, new planet. While I can't confirm if accurate, it does smell amazing.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/006d8aaa3a3597ebca80d5be7a32013bb8b5dd6b-368x366.png)
spritzed by

Nick

Do you live in Teams, Outlook, and SharePoint? We're building Dia's Microsoft tools and we're looking for early testers to help us get them right. You'd have a direct line to the team for debugging and feedback, a first look at new features as they land, and a real hand in shaping where these tools go. results.title: Dia Browser | Pick up where you left off
results.content:
# Pick up where you left off

Over the past six months, hundreds of you have made it clear:

*I love Dia, but I can’t make it my default browser. At least, not until my stuff follows me.*

Starting today, you can bring Dia with you: **Sync** has arrived. Now you can access your favorite parts of your browser, no matter where you are.

These two Dia instances are synced to show you what it looks like across separate machines

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/e330ad3debb8a83270e71ad45704ca436fe944e6-960x960.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

From the desk of

Luan, Software Engineer

Sync sounds simple: all of your stuff, on another machine. But it’s far more complicated than that.

What happens when you rename a tab group on your laptop and delete it on your desktop before they’ve talked to each other? All your stuff, your setup, your profile—gone. You have to start over.

To solve this, we couldn’t just throw everything into a database somewhere. Your data stays encrypted and local-first, which means there’s no server that knows the “right” answer when two machines disagree.

Getting Sync to *just work* meant solving thousands of tiny collisions. But we did it. Sync brings your browser with you—not just the app, but everything you rely on inside it. Now, we can’t wait for you to try it out.

How to set Sync up

Open Dia on your first machine

Go to **Settings → Sync.

**Turn **Sync** on.

You’ll be asked to accept the privacy policy—this allows your data to move with you, while staying encrypted and local-first.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/59ff0087a01bd941bc335c007a377ca940003638-1100x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Create your recovery kit.

Follow the steps and save it somewhere you’ll remember.

***NOTE:*** If you lose both your machine *and* this file, there’s no way to recover your data.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/f4b166d5bbdb09e789bbc6d39557bb0497cd9192-1100x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Open Dia your second machine

Go to **Settings → Sync**.

Turn **Sync** on.

This time, you’ll be asked for a code.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/f12143ca544c496204a3733960c787a658fc03ce-1100x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

Click “Connect Another Device” on your first machine

A 6-character code will appear.

Enter that code on your **second** machine.

![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/f3cfbb9da4aa6aa45bd2a3306f159c836d4d912c-1100x800.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)

That’s it, you’re synced! Give it a second. Your profiles will show up, your bookmarks will settle in, and your browser will start to feel familiar again.

If you need more support on setting Sync up, [**check out this doc**](https://browserinc.notion.site/How-to-set-up-Sync-33c612503676806c82bcfba8920ec7e8) for further instructions or troubleshooting.

### OneLastThing

[Faraz Ghorbanpour ](https://raz-does-art.com/)is a sculptor, animator, and stop-motion artist who makes art *literally* wherever he is. Every day on his commute, he builds these tiny stop-motion stories right in his lap on the train, maybe 10-15 seconds long while the train travels through the city. He’s worked with [Carolina Herrera](https://raz-does-art.com/2025/05/05/commission-carolina-herrera/) and [Patreon](https://raz-does-art.com/2025/05/07/commission-patreon/), was just featured at the Hilton in DC for the Cherry Blossom Festival, and is starting a residency with Nguyen Wahed on April 11th. I think that something I love about his art so much is that it encourages you to re-think *where* you can make art - and the answer is anywhere! No studio needed, and as an artist myself sometimes I forget that the possibilities are truly endless.

![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/b0bdfaae96745615f310c892ddc3f3f0203536e6-626x794.jpg)
admired by

V

[![Dia Browser](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/e5fj2khm/production/bd4e92138780b748f63ad0fd3d9a41eb02da86bd-1080x1676.png?auto=format&q=100&w=800&dpr=2)](https://raz-does-art.com/illustrations/#jp-carousel-1811)
